subject: computer-science
title: Computer Systems: Foundations
welcome_lead: Peek inside the machine — hardware, software and how they meet.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science adventure on hardware, software and the basics of computer systems.
final_note: You now know the building blocks of any computer system.

concepts.def: The physical parts of a computer system.
Programs and data that run on hardware.
Software that manages hardware and apps.
Software for end-user tasks like word processing.
Tools that maintain the system, e.g. backup.
A computer built into another device.

walkthroughs.body_html:
You can touch hardware: keyboard, RAM, CPU. Software is intangible: instructions stored as data.

Without software, hardware does nothing.

• Manages memory and processes
  • Handles files and storage
  • Talks to hardware via device drivers
  • Provides a user interface
  • Enforces security and user accounts
Found in washing machines, traffic lights, microwaves, cars. They are dedicated — one job, done reliably — and often have no screen or keyboard.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between OR and XOR?
options: OR is true when at least one input is true; XOR is true when exactly one input is true.
They are the same gate with different names.
OR is for numbers, XOR is for letters.

mcqs.q: What happens when 11111111 + 1 is computed in an 8-bit register?
options: The computer crashes.
It just becomes 100000000 normally.
Overflow - the result requires 9 bits but only 8 are available.

mcqs.q: How many layers are in the OSI model?
options: The computer crashes.
4 (confusing with TCP/IP model).
7 (Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application).
